newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Allied Domecq saw demerger cost.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Allied Domecq saw demerger cost.

text.p: British spirits, pubs and fast food group Allied Domecq decided against a demerger of its spirits business because of costs and no obvious benefits, chief executive Tony Hales told Reuters Financial Television.

Hales said in an interview to be broadcast on "Inside Equities" at 1145 GMT that costs of such a demerger would be "very, very expensive," adding that it would also have detracted management attention for at least 12 months.
He added that there was "no obvious shareholder value to be unlocked," and that the business had some synergies which gave benefits with the group's retail unit.
He said there was "a lot we can do in terms of improving performance" in both businesses.
Spirits and wines could benefit from increased marketing, improving relations with customers, taking more costs out and improving returns on capital employed.
In the retail sector, expansion in the pub business and cost cutting should push business forward, Hales said.
He said Allied would not be taking "any further major restructuring charges," however.
Allied would hope to secure price increases in line with inflation over the next year in spirits, Hales said, with higher rises in own-brand items balanced by lower increases elsewhere.
"Overall, we are not looking to price increases above the rate of inflation to boost profits," he said.
Hales said the group would like to see dividend cover at a higher level, but added that strong cash flow meant the dividend could be maintained.
Allied Domecq saw pretax, pre-exceptional year profits slip to 575 million stg from 645 million stg previously and paid out a total dividend of 23.59 pence per share.
